Diego / team — answers below, attaching the runbook and the key-ownership matrix. See attachments: redwood_snapshot_runbook_v2.pdf, kms_ownership_matrix.csv.

1) KMS custody model
- Redwood uses a hybrid approach. For Hosted customers (default): snapshots are encrypted with a Redwood-managed KMS key that is Customer-tenant scoped and rotated per our KMS policy; Redwood holds the key material in our KMS tenancy (not exported).
- For Dedicated/private deployments: customers can bring their own key (BYOK) via KMS integrations — in that case Redwood never has plaintext key material and snapshots are encrypted with the customer-managed key.
- For a small subset of legacy integrations (pre-2024 onboarding), there are provider-managed keys where the cloud provider is the KMS custodian. We have an inventory and can flag affected tenants — see kms_ownership_matrix.csv column "key_owner".

2) Snapshots and PII scope
- We treat snapshots as full disk/application-level snapshots of runtime instances. Standard snapshots include application state and persisted data for the tenant.
- We have automated redaction steps for debug traces and ephemeral credentials, but tenant application data is included unless the customer has configured retention/export controls.
- We classify snapshots as potential PII-bearing; when a tenant stores PII in the product, snapshots will include that PII unless the tenant uses encryption-at-application-layer or BYOK.

3) Retention and archival
- Default retention: 30 days for Hosted; Dedicated customers can configure retention (30–90 days typical). Long-term archival requires a separate request and is stored in a locked bucket with restricted access.

4) SOC2 / bridge letter approach
- Redwood can provide our latest SOC 2 Type II report and a bridge letter that references the cloud provider SOC coverage. However, the bridge letter will call out the carve-out scope where the provider holds keys or manages network segmentation.
- For tenants in provider-keyed legacy cases we will explicitly list the affected regions/tenant IDs in the letter to satisfy auditors.

I can prepare a short cover memo that maps CloudScale's questions to the relevant sections of our SOC 2 and the cloud provider report (if we rely on it).

Attachments: redwood_snapshot_runbook_v2.pdf (runbook excerpt), kms_ownership_matrix.csv (inventory of current keys and owners).

Let me know if you want me to draft the bridge letter text for legal/compliance review.

-Mina
